chapter: Absinthe House, Kid Rene and Lee Collins
title: Casey's mother at the dance and the Absinthe House band
summary: A story of a friend bringing his mother to hear the band, then Robinson's praise of the Absinthe House and its four-piece.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: I was there that was crazy with our music I was there. I was there that was crazy with our music I was there. Well, a boy called Craig Casey. He said, Jim, you know what I'm saying? But Casey had bought his sisters. They all loved the band, loved the music and everything. He said, but my mama said, she don't see who I've been running the other band, my daddy, you know what I'm saying? He comes every Saturday and Sunday. He said, I'm not trying to get it out of here. So, that Saturday, so the case had a reserved seat for his mother and his sister. The old man didn't come, you know. He didn't come. He stood up at the house in there. So the daughter and son and a husband and his other sister and his mother came. Oh, and he, when they came in the tables, that's what I'm saying, you know. He made a square, his mother, his mother, his sister, his brother, all of them. And we started playing. So first, we played the first step. He said, she told him, come on, let's go home. I don't like this, I don't understand nothing they're doing. He said, mama, you don't, because you don't go nowhere. He said, you wait. He said, you wait. He said, after a while, we got started playing and shining down there. He said, man, after that. So, they stayed around there, but called after one. It broke about two o'clock, you know, and they left. And the next morning, so he came to our house. He said, man, he said, my mama keep on warning me now. When am I take her back? I told her, I can't take you back tonight, see, because I got to come. You see, your company don't come for me, because I'm your mother, see. You have to take my girl. He said, mom, I can't take you. The girl won't go. No, I can't go. If I can't go, you ain't going. He said, you know, I can't take you back at something tonight. Oh, she said, I love it. I love that music. Man, Casey, man, I was laughing for his mother. Hey, man, you see, his mother, she got big children like that. She looked so young. Young. I thought it was his sister. He said, no, that's my mother, man. Tell me about the absent house. Now, how did that deal work? The absent? Man, that's a beautiful, that's a fine place, and fine people to work for, too. Oh, I could work there. But you're all my life, man. Fine people that don't tell you nothing, and don't know about the past, no remarks, nothing, you know what I mean? It's a natural clean place. Clean, clean place. I love it. Whose band was that, though? Tell me who was in the band, then, when you were there. It was me, at absent house. Yeah. Me, Percy, Emma, and Saif, one of the four of us.
